transcript.text: Our Henry has gone a bit weak and sounds rough, sort of rattly growl instead of the normal hum. It's about 12 years old. Bags and filter are new. Worth fixing?

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. At 12 years old, a Henry vacuum with new bags and filters but weak suction and a rough, rattly growl is often worth fixing if the issue is just a blockage or a simple seal. If it’s an internal motor fault, repair costs might outweigh the value of replacing it. The 'rattly growl' suggests something is either obstructing the airflow (causing the motor to labour) or that the motor bearings are wearing out due to age and strain. Since you’ve already changed the consumables, we need to rule out a blockage first, as this is the most common cause of sudden suction loss and unusual noise. Please check for blockages: detach the hose from the vacuum body and from the wand/floorhead. Look through each section (and the inlet on the floorhead) to ensure nothing like a sock, coin, or large debris is stuck inside. A clear airway should let light through easily. Let me know if you found anything blocked or if everything looked clear.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

I've unplugged it and checked the hose by dropping a coin through, and it went straight through, so the hose seems clear. Suction is weak both at the end of the hose and at the head. What should I check next?

Since the main hose is clear and suction is weak everywhere (including at the head), the blockage is likely further down—either inside the cyclone/bin inlet or deep in the floorhead neck—or, given the 'rattly growl' on a 12-year-old unit, the motor bearings may be wearing out. Please check for an internal blockage next:
1. Remove the dust bag and take out the bin assembly (if removable).
2. Look directly into the main body where the bin sits (the cyclone inlet). Use a torch if needed. Check for small items like coins, buttons, or clumps of debris that might have passed through the hose but got stuck here.
3. Also check the neck on the floorhead/wand where it connects to the main body. If you find something blocked and clear it, try the vacuum again. If these areas are completely clear and the sound remains a rough rattle/growl with weak suction, it is very likely the motor bearings are worn out due to age. In that case, repair is usually not worth it on a 12-year-old Henry, as replacement parts for the motor are often more expensive than a new vacuum.

I'm afraid I'm not sure what I'd be looking for inside the body, as there is only the bag and the tub as far as I can tell. I should also have mentioned that after about five minutes running it gives off a hot, burning electrical smell, and in the dim hall I saw sparks flickering through the grille on top. Is that important?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Yes, that is critically important. Seeing sparks and smelling burning electrical insulation inside the vacuum means there is a serious internal short circuit or wiring fault. This is a fire hazard. Please do not use the Henry again until it has been inspected by a qualified appliance engineer. Repairing this involves opening the casing and working on live mains parts, which is not safe for an owner to attempt. Given the age of the vacuum (12 years) and the severity of the fault, it may be more cost-effective to replace it rather than repair the motor and associated wiring. However, you must have a professional confirm this before proceeding.

candidates: Blockage in hose, wand or floorhead (high)
Worn motor bearings or internal obstruction (medium)
